answer: Cross-held resource ledger. Each identity must hold a unique scarce resource (e.g., a raven-tagged compute slot) verified by two independent peers before transacting. Any duplication attempt reveals itself: the same resource appears in two ledgers, and holders must reconcile via a public ember dispute. An attacker cloning identities must acquire distinct slots per clone, paying full provisioning cost each time, plus a lotus bond forfeited on detected duplication—making the replication cost scale linearly with clone count.
